description:
Follow-ups from the ShortcutColumn port (src/columns/shortcut.rs, ported 2026-08-11 from DWSIM ShortcutColumn.vb @ 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, 9/9 tests green in release, Android check clean).

1. PropertyPackageModel has no one-composition K-value form. Upstream calls DW_CalcKvalue(z, T, P) (ShortcutColumn.vb:201); the port approximates it with ColumnThermo::k_values(z, z, T, P) — exact for Ideal, first-order for cubics. Add a K(z, T, P) entry to the package enum and switch the shortcut (and any future caller) to it.

2. Mixture liquid density (upstream AUX_LIQDENS Rackett route, PropertyPackage.vb:7674) is implemented inline in the shortcut sizing block via Kay's-rule pseudo-criticals into petroleum::aux_props::liquid_density_rackett. Promote a package-level liquid-density entry into crate::thermo so shortcut sizing, pump NPSH inputs, etc. share one implementation.

3. (Optional, NOT upstream) Kirkbride feed-stage correlation as an alternative to the ported Fenske-ratio method — only if a design comparison is wanted; the port is deliberately faithful to upstream, which uses the Fenske ratio (ShortcutColumn.vb:512-519).
title: shortcut column follow-ups: one-composition K-value entry + promote mixture liquid density

description:
THIS IS THE HTR-10 PASSIVE SAFETY CASE and there is no model of it. The scoping doc recommends budgeting for it rather than deferring it indefinitely, because it is the thing that makes the reactor worth simulating.

SCOPE: the heat removal route from bed to reflector to core barrel to reactor pressure vessel to the reactor cavity cooling system, by conduction and radiation, with no forced flow. This is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling without scram, and it is what the safety demonstration tests actually exercise.

Depends on graphite properties and bed effective conductivity — every temperature in this path is set by those two closures.

Also requires trustworthy decay heat, which is currently a separate defect — see the decay-heat bead.
title: HTR-10: reflector, core barrel and cavity-cooling decay-heat path
